name: a brace list expands, with what's around it
mkdir -p makes each directory a list names
lists nest, and an item may be empty
sequences: numbers, letters, padding, steps, downwards
a sequence's ends and step are exact integers, past 2**53 too
a stepped sequence is counted exactly against the limit
a sequence past the limit is an error
a brace with nothing to expand stays literal
quoted or escaped braces stay literal
an escaped comma isn't a separator
find -exec keeps its {}
braces expand before variables
so $N{1,2} names N1 and N2, as in bash
braces inside ${...} stay literal
braces after a default still expand
as in bash, only a nested ${ pairs with a } inside one
a redirect that braces make two of is ambiguous
an ambiguous redirect stops its command before it runs
script: rm victim > f{1,2}; rm victim 2> g{1,2}; rm victim >> h{1,2}; ls
stdout:
f{1,2}: ambiguous redirect
g{1,2}: ambiguous redirect
h{1,2}: ambiguous redirect
victim

name: $PWD is the current directory, after each cd
$PWD is the current directory, whatever the env says
$HOME is the host's
an unset variable stops the script
an unset variable in double quotes too
rm -r $UNSET/x never runs as rm -r /x, nor its rescue
a default reads one that may be unset
a default may hold another expansion
a set variable's default is never read
an unset variable in a default that's read stops the script
single quotes keep a variable literal, set or not
$? is unaffected
arithmetic is named as such, with where it is
error: line 1, col 14: arithmetic expansion $((...)) is not supported

name: an assignment is named as such
error: line 1, col 1: N=3: variable assignment is not supported

name: an assignment before a command too
error: line 2, col 1: N=3: variable assignment is not supported

name: command substitution in double quotes, with where it is
error: line 1, col 9: Command substitution '$(...)' is not supported

name: every problem is reported at once, a loop once
script:
echo ok
for f in a; do echo $f; done
X=1
echo $(pwd)
error:
line 2, col 1: for: control flow is not supported; use xargs or find -exec for iteration
line 3, col 1: X=1: variable assignment is not supported

name: nothing runs when anything is reported
a heredoc problem says where

name: a comment or single quotes may mention them
an assignment as an argument is just a word
